result.method: per-bucket arrayFilter->arraySum + length, then sum(sum)/sum(count) by full ID, then label avg

math: For each original full ID and evaluation time e, avg(samples in (e-window,e] excluding ONLY stale bit payload)=(sum over buckets of sum(filtered values))/(sum over buckets of number of filtered points), with HAVING total filtered count>0. Across time buckets this preserves sample-weighted per-series average rather than equal bucket-weight. Then avg by(stage) across full IDs. Floating-point reduction order changes slightly; exact output parity checked via finite tolerance and NaN classification.
data: Tiny 6-series synthetic TimeSeries including exact stale 0x7ff0000000000002, ordinary NaN 0x7ff8000000000001, stale-only, left-open time boundary, duplicates within and across inserts after OPTIMIZE FINAL; native 5-tick avg by(stage)(avg_over_time[2m]) compared to two SQL plans on same TAGS/SAMPLES
outcome: 22 native output records matched 22 bucket (sum,count) SQL output records including timestamps/stage labels/NaN class/finite values; previous safe arrayJoin SQL also matches; this is a correctness gate, not a speed result
limitations: Bucket-per-ID aggregation still reads/processes every sample. Number of hash aggregation rows may fall but actual CPU, memory and compression must be measured on 2.49m R01.
Only this constrained avg_over_time -> avg by(stage) finite/NaN gauge query; no arbitrary PromQL, multiple labels/offsets/rate/histograms or ACL equivalence.
ClickHouse release O1, no C++ planner patch or 1/4/8 clients.
